part_a_atomicity: No CDP command checks connectedness and assigns files in one renderer task: DOM.setFileInputFiles is a DOM-domain command that the page cannot gate (a Runtime.callFunctionOn cannot set files from paths), and Chromium's assignment fires input/change on the node whether or not it is connected (the wave-3 mock models this at browser/v2_tests.rs:543-549; the REAL F'S/F5 cells observe it). Pausing the page (Page.setWebLifecycleState frozen, Emulation.setScriptExecutionDisabled, a Debugger pause) would change page-visible behaviour or suppress the page's own listeners, so it is not a candidate. F5 therefore closes the RECEIPT (re-check the same objectId after the assignment; detached -> refused browser_ref_stale with detail delivery=unknown, retryable=false) and leaves the EFFECT window irreducible.
part_a_receipt_mapping_limit: action_record.rs:663-677 (legacy_effect) maps every status=refused receipt to effect=refused, including this delivery-unknown one; the same holds for the pre-existing trusted-click cleanup case (tools.rs:1316-1324). The receipt itself carries delivery=unknown, retryable=false; both jev-use runners never re-dispatch on retryable=false (python/run.py:111, typescript/run.ts:134-137).

The reader itself is not session-checked: if a future schema admits snapshot_id it must take the caller's session (the draft ea12e6f86 does this; not in F5).
